To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the anti-Candida immune response is highly complex and involves the coordinated action of multiple cell types, which are regulated by multiple signaling pathways and transcription factors.

(i) the immune system is capable to mount an efficient response against Candida infections, (ii) the response is complex and depends on the host, the Candida species and the type of infection, (iii) the immune response is orchestrated by a complex regulatory network of transcription factors and signaling pathways that is influenced by the host and Candida species, (iv) the response involves both pro- and anti-inflammatory pathways and (v) the response is influenced by other commensal microbiota.
the host response to Candida is complex and that a systems approach is needed for understanding this complexity.

the development of new methods for the analysis of biological systems.
the development of a systems biology approach to study the host response to Candida infection, with a particular focus on the role of the microbiome in shaping the host response.
the development of novel diagnostic and therapeutic tools based on omics data.
